subject.title: feat(memory): graduate sessionMemory from experimental — solve the multi-session continuity problem

question: Should session transcript indexing remain experimental opt-in, graduate as stable opt-in, or become default-on for new installs after privacy/source-policy gates?
rationale: The code path exists, but changing the feature contract or default affects sensitive transcript indexing, cross-channel visibility, QMD parity, and user cost expectations; automation cannot choose that policy safely.

options.title: Graduate stable opt-in first
options.body: Keep it off by default while removing the experimental framing only after docs, privacy, QMD, source-label, duplicate-indexing, and cost guidance are complete.

options.title: Keep experimental until blockers close
options.body: Leave the current experimental opt-in untouched until concrete issues such as gateway-dispatched session recall and duplicate raw/summary hits are resolved.

options.title: Default on for new installs
options.body: Enable it for new installs only with explicit DM-only/privacy defaults, upgrade docs, live proof, and opt-out/doctor guidance.

recommendation.title: Graduate stable opt-in first
recommendation.body: Keep it off by default while removing the experimental framing only after docs, privacy, QMD, source-label, duplicate-indexing, and cost guidance are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the experimental source and has the strongest sampled history across the central memory/session files.
